verdict.rationale: Extend lets users create API keys from Developer settings, and its test-mode API keys are confined to an isolated environment that never touches production data or fires production webhooks. That is a coarse, environment-level form of credential scoping. There is no evidence of per-key permission scopes, resource restrictions, or agent-specific credentials. Advanced RBAC and MCP tool limiting are adjacent controls and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: per-key permission/resource scopes, read-only or endpoint-restricted keys, agent-dedicated credential issuance, key expiry/rotation docs, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Create an API key from your Developer settings
Runs made with a test API key never touch production data and never fire production webhooks
Use a test-mode API key to run extractions, classifications, and workflows against an isolated test environment with no production data or webhooks.
